title: Whole-mount staining coupled to a UV-inducible basal cell carcinoma murine model
protocol: Heat 800 mL of PBS to 60°C in a beaker and keep it on a heat plate at 60°C in a ventilated hood.
Add 40 g of paraformaldehyde powder to the heated PBS solution.
Slowly raise the pH to 7 by adding 1 N NaOH dropwise until the solution clears.
Adjust the volume of the fixation solution to 1 L with PBS and aliquot or freeze for storage at 2°C–8°C for up to 1 month.
Add 200 mL of 1× PBS to a glass beaker on a stir plate.
Add 40 g of sucrose powder to the PBS solution and stir until dissolved.
Store the 20% sucrose solution at 2°C–8°C for up to 1 month.
Dissolve 0.2 g of BSA in 6.85 mL of PBS.
Add 50 μL of Triton X, 2 mL of normal goat serum (NGS), 100 μL of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and 1 mL of 1 M maleic acid (pH 7.5) to the BSA solution.
Dissolve 0.2 g of BSA in 8.85 mL of PBS.
Add 50 μL of Triton X and 100 μL of DMSO to the mixture.
Add 1 mL of 1 M maleic acid (pH 7.5) to complete the diluent solution preparation.
For washing solution, add 5 mL of Triton X and 5 mL Tween 20 in 990 mL of PBS.
Prepare DAPI solution by adding 1 μL of DAPI to 999 μL of 1× PBS.
Collect skin from storage place.
Place the skin in a Petri dish if stored at -80°C.
Leave the tissue between 20°C and 25°C for 20 minutes or until thawed.
Use a scalpel to gently scrape away fat and blood vessels covering the dermis until clearly exposed.
Gently scrape away hypodermis (fat) and blood vessels using a scalpel.
Prepare small pieces of back skin (5 mm² maximum).
Place the samples in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube with 500 μL of blocking solution.
Rock the tube on a tube roller mixer between 20°C and 25°C for 5 hours.
Transfer the samples to a new Eppendorf tube with 200 μL primary antibody diluted in diluent solution.
Rock the tube on a tube roller mixer at 4°C between 14 and 16 hours.
Place the samples in a new Eppendorf tube with 300 μL of washing buffer.
Place tubes on a tube roller mixer between 20°C and 25°C for 30 minutes.
Repeat steps 13 and 14 three times.
Place the skin pieces in a new Eppendorf tube containing 300 μL secondary antibody diluted in diluent solution.
Place tubes in a dark chamber or cover with aluminum foil.
Collect tissues using forceps with minimal pressure.
Rock the tube on a tube roller mixer at 4°C between 14 h and 16 h.
Transfer samples to new Eppendorf tube with 300 μL of washing buffer.
Rock the tube on a tube roller mixer between 20°C and 25°C for 30 min.
Repeat steps involving rocking, transferring, and mixing five times.
Transfer samples to new Eppendorf tube with 300 μL of DAPI solution.
Rock the tube on a tube roller mixer at 4°C between 14 h and 16 h.
Transfer samples to new Eppendorf tube with 100 μL of clearing buffer.
Incubate samples for at least 3 h between 20°C and 25°C.
Remove excess clearing buffer with a tissue.
Place skin pieces in the middle of a concave slide.
Mount up to four pieces of 5 mm² on a single slide.
Using a fluorescent microscope, ensure the epidermis is facing up.
Flip pieces that are not properly orientated.
Cover the samples with 2–3 drops of mounting media.
Gently apply the coverslip at an angle to avoid bubbles.
Apply light pressure on the coverslip to evenly spread the mounting media and remove bubbles from the tissue.
Seal the coverslip on the slide using nail polish.
